title: Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements): One Agreement per Service Account and Fixed Terms
content:
**Board Policy, Credit and Collections — Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements): agreements held by one member**

**1. Scope of an agreement.** A member may hold agreements on several service accounts. Each agreement covers the past-due amount of one service account only, and past-due amounts of different service accounts are never combined into one agreement. The cooperative sets no limit on how many agreements one member may hold across separate service accounts.

**2. One open agreement per service account.** A service account may carry at most the tier's limit of agreements in offered or active status at a time (the limit appears in the limits table of the Payment Arrangements tiers). The test is made on the cooperative's own arrangement records for that service account before an offer is made: an agreement already standing in offered status, or in active status, on the same service account counts; agreements on the member's other service accounts do not count toward this service account's limit.

**3. Terms fixed while the agreement runs.** The terms of an active agreement are never changed while it runs, because no tier allows renegotiation. A member who cannot keep the agreement defaults, and the default rules apply.

**Application of section 2 (hypothetical records, limit of one at a time)**

| Agreements already on the same service account | Limit of one at a time |
|---|---|
| none | not reached |
| one in offered status | reached — no further offer on this service account |
| one in active status | reached — no further offer on this service account |
| only agreements in completed, defaulted, expired or terminated status | not reached, none of them being offered or active |
| one active agreement on a different service account of the same member | not reached on this service account |

**Application of section 1** — for a hypothetical member with a past-due farm home account and a past-due shop meter account, any agreement covers the past-due amount of one of the two accounts only; a single agreement spreading the two past-due amounts together is never offered.
